import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. LOAD DATA
crime_path = "chunks_csv/outlierr/2023_crime.csv"
adj_path   = "chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv"

crime_df = pd.read_csv(crime_path)            # columns: borough, Crime_value
adj_df   = pd.read_csv(adj_path)              # columns: borough, neighbor
crime_df.set_index('borough', inplace=True)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. BUILD AN UNDIRECTED ADJACENCY LOOK-UP  (dict: borough -> set(neighbors))
adjacency = {b:set() for b in crime_df.index}
for b, n in adj_df.itertuples(index=False):
    if b in adjacency and n in adjacency:     # retain only boroughs that exist in crime_df
        adjacency[b].add(n)
        adjacency[n].add(b)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
def compute_neighbor_means(current_df):
    """
    Given current_df (index: borough, col Crime_value), return Series of neighbor means,
    considering only boroughs present in current_df.
    """
    present = set(current_df.index)
    means = {}
    for b in current_df.index:
        nbhrs = adjacency[b].intersection(present)
        if nbhrs:                     # at least one neighbour still present
            means[b] = current_df.loc[list(nbhrs), 'Crime_value'].mean()
        else:                         # no valid neighbours; set NaN so row will be dropped
            means[b] = np.nan
    return pd.Series(means, name='NeighborMean')

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. ITERATIVE-R PROCEDURE TO REDUCE MASKING
df_current = crime_df.copy()
max_iter = 10
cutoff_z = 2.5
for _ in range(max_iter):
    neighbor_mean = compute_neighbor_means(df_current)
    df_model = df_current.join(neighbor_mean)
    df_model = df_model.dropna(subset=['NeighborMean'])   # rows lacking neighbour mean removed
    # Linear regression Crime = b0 + b1 * NeighborMean
    X = np.vstack([np.ones(len(df_model)), df_model['NeighborMean'].values]).T
    y = df_model['Crime_value'].values
    beta, _, _, _ = np.linalg.lstsq(X, y, rcond=None)
    y_hat = X @ beta
    residuals = y - y_hat
    sigma = residuals.std(ddof=1)
    z_scores = residuals / sigma
    df_model = df_model.assign(residual=residuals, z=z_scores)

    # Identify outliers
    outliers = df_model.index[abs(df_model['z']) > cutoff_z]
    # Stop if no new outliers
    if len(outliers) == 0:
        df_current = df_model  # final dataset for later stats
        break
    # Otherwise, drop them and iterate again
    df_current = df_current.drop(index=outliers)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. FINAL STATISTICS FOR WESTMINSTER
westminster_z = df_current.loc['Westminster', 'z'] if 'Westminster' in df_current.index else np.nan

# Classification
if np.isnan(westminster_z):
    verdict = "NOT AN OUTLIER"   # Westminster was removed as an extreme outlier earlier
elif westminster_z >= cutoff_z:
    verdict = "OUTLIER - HIGH"
elif westminster_z <= -cutoff_z:
    verdict = "OUTLIER - LOW"
else:
    verdict = "NOT AN OUTLIER"

data_points_used = len(df_current)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. PRINT RESULTS
print(f"data_points_used = {data_points_used}")
print(f"FINAL ANSWER: {verdict} (z = {westminster_z:.3f})")

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import math

# -------------------------------
# 1. LOAD DATA
# -------------------------------
CRIME_PATH = 'chunks_csv/outlierr/2023_crime.csv'
ADJ_PATH   = 'chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv'

crime_df = pd.read_csv(CRIME_PATH)               # columns: borough, Crime_value
adj_df   = pd.read_csv(ADJ_PATH)                 # columns: borough, neighbor

# -------------------------------------------------
# 2. BUILD UNDIRECTED NEIGHBOUR LIST (as dict set)
# -------------------------------------------------
neighbors = {b: set() for b in crime_df['borough']}

for _, row in adj_df.iterrows():
    b1, b2 = row['borough'], row['neighbor']
    neighbors.setdefault(b1, set()).add(b2)
    neighbors.setdefault(b2, set()).add(b1)      # ensure symmetry

# Convenience: series for quick value lookup
value_series = crime_df.set_index('borough')['Crime_value']

# -------------------------------------------------
# 3. ITERATIVE-R   (Lu, Chen & Kou, 2003)
# -------------------------------------------------
sample_set       = set(crime_df['borough'])      # currently “kept” boroughs
prev_outliers    = set()
threshold        = 2.5
epsilon          = 1e-9                          # guards σ = 0
max_iter         = 100

for _ in range(max_iter):
    # --- 3a. spatial lag for every borough still in the sample
    lag_vals = {}
    for b in sample_set:
        nbrs = [n for n in neighbors[b] if n in sample_set]
        lag_vals[b] = np.mean([value_series[n] for n in nbrs]) if nbrs else np.nan
    lag_s = pd.Series(lag_vals, name='Lag')

    # --- 3b. regression dataset
    reg_df = pd.DataFrame({
        'Crime': value_series.loc[list(sample_set)],
        'Lag'  : lag_s
    }).dropna()                                  # drops rows with no neighbours

    # --- 3c. OLS:  Crime = β0 + β1 * Lag
    X = np.vstack([np.ones(len(reg_df)), reg_df['Lag'].values]).T
    y = reg_df['Crime'].values
    beta = np.linalg.lstsq(X, y, rcond=None)[0]  # β0, β1

    y_hat = X @ beta
    residuals = y - y_hat
    sigma = residuals.std(ddof=2) or epsilon

    z_scores = pd.Series(residuals / sigma, index=reg_df.index)

    # --- 3d. detect outliers in this iteration
    current_outliers = set(z_scores[ z_scores.abs() > threshold ].index)

    # convergence check
    if current_outliers == prev_outliers:
        break
    # update for next loop
    sample_set -= current_outliers
    prev_outliers = current_outliers.copy()
else:
    raise RuntimeError("Iterative-R failed to converge in allotted iterations.")

# --------------------------------------------
# 4.  FINAL WESTMINSTER TEST STATISTIC
# --------------------------------------------
west = 'Westminster'

# Re-compute neighbour lag for Westminster,
#   but exclude any boroughs removed in final sample_set
west_neighbors = [n for n in neighbors[west] if n in sample_set]
west_lag = np.mean([value_series[n] for n in west_neighbors])

# Predicted crime & residual
west_y     = value_series[west]
west_y_hat = beta[0] + beta[1] * west_lag
west_resid = west_y - west_y_hat
west_z     = west_resid / sigma

# Two-tailed p-value from standard normal
p_value = math.erfc(abs(west_z)/math.sqrt(2))

# Verdict

elif west_z < -threshold: verdict = 'OUTLIER - LOW'
else:                     verdict = 'NOT AN OUTLIER'

# ---------------------------
# 5.  PRINT REQUIRED LINES

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# -----------------------------
# 1. Load data
# -----------------------------
crime_path = 'chunks_csv/outlierr/2023_crime.csv'
adj_path   = 'chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv'

crime_df   = pd.read_csv(crime_path)              # columns: borough, Crime_value
adj_df     = pd.read_csv(adj_path)                # columns: borough, neighbor

# Ensure borough names are stripped for safe look-ups
crime_df['borough'] = crime_df['borough'].str.strip()
adj_df['borough']   = adj_df['borough'].str.strip()
adj_df['neighbor']  = adj_df['neighbor'].str.strip()

# -----------------------------
# 2. Build a symmetric neighbour dictionary
# -----------------------------
neigh_dict = {b:set() for b in crime_df['borough']}
for _, row in adj_df.iterrows():
    b1, b2 = row['borough'], row['neighbor']
    if b1 in neigh_dict and b2 in neigh_dict:     # guard against stray names
        neigh_dict[b1].add(b2)
        neigh_dict[b2].add(b1)                    # make symmetric

# -----------------------------
# Helper: spatial lag
# -----------------------------
def spatial_lag(values, sample_set):
    """
    values: pd.Series indexed by borough, containing Crime_value
    sample_set: set of boroughs currently retained
    Returns: pd.Series (same index as sample_set) of neighbour means, NaN if no neighbours in sample_set.
    """
    lags = {}
    for b in sample_set:
        nbs = neigh_dict[b].intersection(sample_set)
        if len(nbs) == 0:
            lags[b] = np.nan
        else:
            lags[b] = values.loc[list(nbs)].mean()
    return pd.Series(lags)

# -----------------------------
# 3. ITERATIVE-R loop
# -----------------------------
all_boroughs      = set(crime_df['borough'])
sample_set        = all_boroughs.copy()        # boroughs currently in the model
previous_outliers = set()
threshold         = 2.5                        # |z| > 2.5 ⇒ outlier

while True:
    # Current data subset
    y_full = crime_df.set_index('borough')['Crime_value']
    y      = y_full.loc[list(sample_set)]
    
    # Compute spatial lag for current sample
    L = spatial_lag(y_full, sample_set)
    
    # Drop rows with NaN spatial lag (no neighbours left)
    valid_idx = L.dropna().index
    y_valid   = y.loc[valid_idx]
    L_valid   = L.loc[valid_idx]
    
    # Design matrix with intercept
    X = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(L_valid)), L_valid.values])
    
    # OLS coefficients: beta = (X'X)^{-1} X'y
    beta, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(X, y_valid.values, rcond=None)
    y_hat    = X @ beta
    residuals= y_valid.values - y_hat
    sigma    = residuals.std(ddof=1)
    if sigma == 0:
        sigma = 1e-9
    
    z_scores = residuals / sigma
    current_outliers = set(valid_idx[np.abs(z_scores) > threshold])
    
    # Check convergence
    if not current_outliers or current_outliers == previous_outliers:
        final_beta   = beta
        final_sigma  = sigma
        final_sample = set(valid_idx)           # Final regression sample
        break
    
    # Otherwise iterate
    previous_outliers = current_outliers
    sample_set -= current_outliers              # Remove detected outliers and repeat

# 4. Compute Westminster statistic (using final model)
# -----------------------------
westminster = 'Westminster'
y_full      = crime_df.set_index('borough')['Crime_value']
west_y      = y_full.loc[westminster]

# Spatial lag for Westminster using ONLY neighbours still in final_sample
west_neighs = neigh_dict[westminster].intersection(final_sample)
if len(west_neighs) == 0:
    west_L = np.nan
else:
    west_L = y_full.loc[list(west_neighs)].mean()

# Predicted value & z-score
if np.isnan(west_L):
    # Cannot evaluate – treat as zero influence
    west_pred = final_beta[0]
else:
    west_pred = final_beta[0] + final_beta[1] * west_L

west_res   = west_y - west_pred
west_z     = west_res / final_sigma

# -----------------------------
# 5. Classify Westminster
# -----------------------------
if west_z > threshold:
    verdict = 'OUTLIER - HIGH'
elif west_z < -threshold:
    verdict = 'OUTLIER - LOW'
else:
    verdict = 'NOT AN OUTLIER'

# -----------------------------
# 6. Reporting
# -----------------------------
data_points_used = len(final_sample)

print(f"data_points_used = {data_points_used}")
print(f"FINAL ANSWER: {verdict} (z = {west_z})")
